variants.title: Cryogenic thermometry: a Pt100 platinum resistance thermometer
variants.method: calibration against the cryostat set-point; excitation 100 uA
variants.unknown: sensitivity dR/dT and the self-heating error
variants.note: R = R0 (1 + A t + B t^2 + C (t - 100) t^3) for t below 0 C, with the IEC 60751 constants; R0 = 100 ohm. About 0.2 ohm per kelvin at 77 K, so the readout needs micro-ohm resolution.

source.title: IEC 60751: A = 3.9083e-3 /C, B = -5.775e-7 /C^2, C = -4.183e-12 /C^4 (industrial platinum resistance thermometers)

variants.title: Cryogenic thermometry: a RuO2 thick-film resistor near 20 K (illustrative)
variants.sample: RuO2 thick-film resistor, R = 1 kohm x exp(sqrt(20 K / T)) (unsourced / illustrative)
variants.method: calibration against the cryostat set-point; excitation 1 uA
variants.unknown: sensitivity dR/dT and the self-heating error
variants.note: Variable-range-hopping form: the resistance climbs steeply as the sensor cools, so it is most sensitive below about 30 K. The prefactor and T0 are illustrative.

source.title: Unsourced / illustrative sample constants
source.note: the form ln R ~ sqrt(T0/T) is textbook hopping; Rinf and T0 are chosen for the lab, not looked up.

variants.title: Cryogenic thermometry: a thermocouple against a 300 K junction
variants.sample: Thermocouple pair with Seebeck S = 40 uV/K x T/(T + 60 K) (unsourced / illustrative)
variants.method: calibration against the cryostat set-point; reference junction at 300 K
variants.note: Its sensitivity falls towards zero as T tends to zero, so a thermocouple is a poor thermometer in the helium range. The law is illustrative, not a standard table.

source.title: Unsourced / illustrative sample constants
source.note: the Seebeck law is a smooth illustrative one; no standard thermocouple table was used.
